articles.title: Manchester United vs Tottenham: Different summer transfer strategies collide on Saturday at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Tottenham spent more than double what Manchester United did on new signings in the summer transfer window; despite differing strategies, both clubs have had poor starts to their seasons as the pair meet at Old Trafford in the Premier League on Saturday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Two clubs with very different strategies in the summer now find themselves facing a remarkably similar problem after underwhelming starts to the season, as the pair meet at Old Trafford in the Premier League on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

Spurs spent £334m, including £100m on Sandro Tonali, as Roberto De Zerbi was handed significant backing to reshape his squad.

United, by contrast, were more frugal with their spending, with £163m committed to their rebuild.

Yet ahead of this weekend's crunch game, Spurs sit bottom of the Premier League and are still waiting for their first win, while Michael Carrick is already feeling the pressure at Old Trafford.

The scrutiny, then, cannot simply be confined to the two managers. At both clubs, the contrasting decisions made above them this summer are beginning to demand examination.

Man Utd yet to break £100m mark on a single player

Manchester United have refused to follow the modern Premier League trend of putting £100m-plus into one statement signing, but that is not understood to reflect a reluctance to spend. Instead, it reflects the club's approach to rebuilding the squad.

As Sky Sports News' Dan Khan explains, the £100m figure itself can be misleading.

"I actually think it's redundant to use that figure of £100m. If you look at appreciation, Paul Pogba, if you were to sign him now from Juventus, like United did, that would probably be well over £100m.

"The question is, can Man Utd spend money on Elliot Anderson? Not necessarily to do with the figure but more whether they are in the market for these top midfielders.

United's priority this summer was midfield, with three additions needed rather than one marquee arrival. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba have therefore accounted for much of the spending.

A left-back was also considered, with United monitoring Myles Lewis-Skelly and Lewis Hall, but neither was realistically available. Instead, the club doubled down on midfield, with the expectation that left-back will be addressed next summer.

There is also a need for United to improve their ability to sell. "Their most senior sales were Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek, who hadn't played a senior game," Khan says. "I don't think there is a reluctance to spend big, having spoken to people in and around the club. But it was quite clear that this summer they needed to increase the squad size to compete in different competitions."

The result is a deliberate preference for squad depth over one blockbuster signing. Whether that proves to be strategic patience or an incomplete rebuild will depend heavily on the results.

Why the pressure should not solely be on Carrick

Carrick is the man on the touchline, but the scrutiny at United will begin to climb up the chain.

For Khan, the focus will move onto director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, who have been entrusted with leading the Sir Jim Ratcliffe era.

"There will be a big microscope on Wilcox and Berrada, especially because they have been trusted in leading this Ratcliffe era forward. They went out on a limb to appoint Ruben Amorim. It must be said, they gave him a lot of time."

That managerial history is significant. Under the current regime, United have gone from Erik ten Hag to Amorim to Carrick, yet Khan does not expect another sudden change.

"When we are talking about Carrick, I wouldn't imagine any sudden decisions will be made on his future. First of all, they all decided to give Ten Hag a new contract. Then they pivoted to Amorim and then they went out for Carrick."

But that does not mean the hierarchy escapes scrutiny.

"I'm not saying that's a bad decision. However, when the slogan is that we are 'going for the best in class and we're doing everything data driven,' I can't imagine Ratcliffe is very happy at the moment in terms of the results and the performances."

Despite spending more than double on signings than Man Utd, Spurs have made their worst start to a Premier League season after five games.

They head to Old Trafford still searching for their first league win of the season, and their dismal start has already raised questions over their lavish summer spending.

Asked on a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast whether any of the 10 new recruits have impressed, ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood replied: "No, no one," he insisted. "I can't say anyone's really impressed me, and anyone would have done a better job than anyone who was there last season.

"They've underachieved, they really have. We always judge on results, so I don't look at any individual player and think, 'well, you're coming out of some credit here', because the team's losing, and I'm not sure there's been any outstanding performers."

The lack of success from Spurs' signings before this summer worries Sherwood about the latest recruits.

"Probably the last four or five years, the track record of Tottenham signings has not been fantastic," he said.

"It's been a very long time since they've made a decent signing. Now, I'm not saying they're poor signings; I'm saying that they haven't done it yet, and there's still a lot of time to be able to get some confidence and show what they can really do.

"We've seen them in fits and starts and little cameos for other teams, but it's a different kettle of fish playing for Tottenham."

Following the summer arrivals, De Zerbi has more options at his disposal, but that appears to have led to indecision around his best starting XI.

The Italian has made the most changes to starting XIs in the Premier League this season (13).

Sherwood said: "If you were a Man Utd fan and Bruno Fernandes was missing, you'd be devastated.

"But I'm not sure any Tottenham fans would be devastated if any of their players are missing, because I'm not sure the manager knows their best team at the moment.

"The fans certainly don't, and you're asking me, and I don't!"

Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge believes the squad is still short in two areas, despite their huge summer spending.

He told a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast: "I think they need a striker - an actual No 9 - but how many are there out there?

"It doesn't help that Will Lankshear is scoring every week for Middlesbrough because he looks like a proper old-fashioned centre-forward and he's young and English. That's my worry.

"I'm also not 100 per cent sure if Antonin Kinsky is a Tottenham No 1 for years to come.

"He did an incredible job keeping the club in the Premier League with his saves. However, I'm still not sure if he's still a No 1.

"If you've spent that amount of money and you still need, for me, a goalkeeper and a No 9, then there's still a way to go."

articles.title: Messi comienza su 'nueva' vida
articles.standfirst: Regresó a los entrenamientos con Inter Miami tras despedirse de la selección argentina
articles.summary: Regresó a los entrenamientos con Inter Miami tras despedirse de la selección argentina
articles.body: No han pasado ni 48 horas desde que el Monumental de Buenos Aires fuese testigo del último partido de Leo Messi con Argentina. No había tiempo que perder... y el rosarino ya ha empezado la que será su 'nueva' vida hasta que decida 'colgar las botas'. "Ya está todo dicho. Y ahora, todo está hecho", podía leerse en un 'post' publicado por Leo para, ahora sí, cerrar un capítulo de leyenda con la 'Albiceleste' que ha durado 21 años. "Las únicas palabras que me salen del corazón son: gracias, Argentina", sentenciaba con una imagen en la que se le ve levantando su camiseta con la '10'. Han sido días repletos de emoción que jamás olvidará. Pero no quiere quedarse a vivir en ese recuerdo y, por ello, ha tratado de cambiar el 'chip' lo antes posible. Cogió un vuelo de vuelta a Estados Unidos y ya se ha puesto a las órdenes del 'Kily' González en las filas de Inter Miami. El propio club ha compartido contenido en redes mostrando que el astro argentino ya está de vuelta a los entrenamientos. Más allá del triunfo en la Campeones Cup contra Cruz Azul, Leo Messi quiere estar a disposición tras el parón de cara al duelo contra DC United en casa. Un compromiso que, a siete jornadas de finalizar la temporada regular en la MLS, se antoja clave. Inter Miami, tercero en la Conferencia Este, se marchó al parón con derrota ante Colombus Crew y ya enlaza cinco fechas sin ganar... y una única victoria en las últimas 10. No será por Leo Messi, que presume de ser el jugador con más goles (21) y asistencias (11) en lo que marcha de temporada. A sus 39 años, está realizando otro curso de MVP. Sin embargo, necesita que el equipo acompañe para intentar arrebatarle a New England la segunda plaza y tener, a priori, un enfrentamiento más favorable en 'playoffs' para iniciar la reválida del título. El día que se canse de ganar... será el momento de decir adiós. Todavía no ha llegado y, a partir de hoy, arranca su 'nueva' vida.

articles.title: ¿Te acuerdas de LaLiga? Los 19 días más largos
articles.standfirst: Te recordamos todo lo que pasó antes del gran parón de selecciones
articles.summary: Te recordamos todo lo que pasó antes del gran parón de selecciones
articles.body: Tras tres semanas (19 días exactamente) en las que el fútbol de naciones ha ocupado todas las portadas (la selección española intratable, el incidente de Cristiano Ronaldo, etc.), en el parón de selecciones más largo de la historia (sin contar el Mundial), algunos aficionados han podido perder el hilo de lo que sucedió en las siete jornadas de LaLiga disputadas hasta el momento. El Fútbol Club Barcelona se marchó al parón de selecciones como primer clasificado de la competición, después de hacer un arranque espectacular. Los de Hansi Flick han hecho pleno de victorias. Pero además, sumando goleada tras goleada. En los siete partidos han logrado anotar 31 goles. Una media de 4,43 goles por encuentro. 13 tantos más que el segundo equipo más goleador, el Real Madrid. Frente a Elche, Valencia y Racing lograron una diferencia de cinco goles. Un gran rendimiento ofensivo que sirve para contrarrestar los siete tantos recibidos, uno por partido de media. En cuatro jornadas ha visto el Barcelona profanada sus redes. Sin embargo la avalancha goleadora ha provocado que se sitúen en lo alto de la tabla y busquen el tercer título consecutivo. En la última jornada antes del parón tuvo lugar el derbi madrileño, que enfrentó a Atlético de Madrid y Real Madrid. Un encuentro que como de costumbre fue caliente, y la polémica estuvo servida. Los madridistas protestaron las acciones de Romero sobre Bellingham, en la que el argentino pisó la rodilla del inglés tras intentar jugar el balón; y la de Kang-In Lee sobre Valverde, en la que el surcoreano entró con dureza sobre el tobillo del uruguayo. La primera fue sancionada con tarjeta amarilla tras revisión del VAR. Pero la segunda ni fue revisada, solo se castigó con falta. En la segunda parte, el Madrid se quedó con 10 tras el agarrón de Huijsen a Giuliano en el área. Los rojiblancos consiguieron ponerse con ventaja de dos, gracias a los tantos de Grimaldo y Jonathan David. El gol de Rüdiger no consiguió rascar puntos para los blancos. Una derrota que mandó a los merengues a la cuarta posición, después de Barcelona, el propio Atlético, y el Betis. En las primeras jornadas surgieron muchos candidatos a hacerse con el premio Pichichi. Sin embargo, Raphinha se encargó antes del parón de adelantarse a la competencia. El brasileño marcó seis goles en las últimas dos jornadas, contra Racing y Sevilla, estableciéndose con 12 tantos como líder en solitario por el premio al goleador de LaLiga. Con cinco goles de diferencia hay un triple empate entre Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé y Sergio Camello. El '10' del Barça comenzó su carrera goleadora en la tercera jornada frente al Rayo, marcando en cuatro partidos consecutivos, aunque frente al Sevilla acabó la racha. El francés, ganador de los dos últimos Pichichi, ha metido en todos los partidos que el Madrid ha ganado esta temporada, excepto el debut liguero contra el Rayo. Sin embargo, en las derrotas contra Betis y Atlético de Madrid no pudo aparecer, lo que ha lastrado su participación en el premio individual. Por su parte, Camello está firmando su mejor, no solo arranque, sino curso goleador de su carrera en Primera. La temporada que más tantos metió en la máxima competición española fue la 22/23, con seis anotaciones. Esta campaña, siete goles en siete partidos, compitiendo de tú a tú a los mejores delanteros del mundo. Tras estas figuras aparecen otros arietes con seis tantos como Roberto Fernández, que su buen arranque le ha servido para acudir a la Selección española; Yassir Zabiri, que cinco de sus seis goles han sido para lograr las dos victorias del Racing; y con cinco, como Aubameyang, que ha llevado al Dépor a pelear por puestos europeos, aunque el gabonés tendrá que esperar para continuar en la carrera por su lesión en el menisco. Ya se han mencionado los equipos que están clasificados actualmente para Champions. Pero las plazas de Europa League y Conference League están ocupadas por dos equipos que en los últimos han estado más pendientes de no descender: Sevilla y Alavés. La pasada temporada estos conjuntos se salvaron de bajar por un solo punto. Y en esta, si se terminase en este momento, el próximo año representarían al país por el continente. El Sevilla, en el puesto de su competición fetiche, tan solo ha cedido los tres puntos en dos ocasiones, contra Barcelona y Atlético de Madrid, los dos primeros clasificados. Al igual que el Alavés, que solo ha perdido frente a Racing y Valencia. Aunque los vascos han empatado dos encuentros, mientras que los andaluces solo uno. Pero en la competición no solo hay parte buena. Cada año tres equipos tienen que despedirse de la élite española. Tras siete jornadas, los equipos que ocupan esas plazas son Elche, Valencia y Málaga. El mal rendimiento defensivo de los ilicitanos ha llevado a que caigan hasta el decimoséptimo puesto. Son el segundo equipo que más goles ha recibido, 17, solo superado por el Racing. Aunque en la última jornada sumaron la primera victoria de la temporada en casa del Espanyol. Un triunfo que esperan que sea el primero de muchos si quieren continuar en Primera. Los dos acompañantes en los puestos de descenso han recibido algunos goles menos, pero su producción ofensiva es mucho menor. El Valencia sacó tres puntos de oro de Mendizorroza en la sexta jornada, y cerca estuvieron de puntuar contra la Real Sociedad en Mestalla en la séptima, pero el gol en el descuento de Barrenetxea les privó de un punto que puede ser crucial en el futuro. Pero ahora encaran la temporada con un nuevo entrenador, Javier Aguirre. El Málaga como colista está viviendo un sueño amargo. Tras varios años lejos de la máxima categoría, han regresado esta temporada, pero las cosas no estás saliendo como planeaban. Todavía no saben lo que es ganar, ya que sus tres puntos proceden de los empates frente a Dépor, Levante y Celta. Una competición que vuelve tras casi tres semanas de parón.

articles.title: Tottenham: Xavi Simons enrols at Harvard University while out injured
articles.summary: Tottenham's Xavi Simons enrols at prestigious American university Harvard as he continues his recovery from a long-term injury.
articles.body:
Tottenham midfielder Xavi Simons has enrolled on a course at prestigious American university Harvard while he continues his recovery from a long-term knee injury.

The 23-year-old Netherlands playmaker has been sidelined since rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament in April - an injury that forced him to miss the World Cup.

Simons has now joined , external Harvard's Crossover into Business programme, a course tailored for professional athletes to develop their commercial skills.

The online course pairs athletes with Harvard MBA students to mentor them through practical case studies and enterprise management.

"I'm going back to school," Simons wrote on LinkedIn.

"During my recovery, I've been trying to use my time in the best way possible. Football is still my main focus, but I also want to keep learning and improving away from the pitch.

"I've always been interested in more than just football. I want to understand the business side of the game better, learn from people in different industries and keep developing as a person."

Simons recently travelled to the United States to step up his physical rehabilitation while visiting Harvard's campus in Boston.

"Getting back on the pitch is still my number one priority," Simons added.

"At the same time, I want to use this period to keep learning and invest in myself beyond football. Looking forward to getting started."

Previous participants on the Crossover into Business programme have included players from the NBA, NFL, and tennis, including former world number one and two-time major champion Victoria Azarenka.

In June, Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga took a short course at Harvard in the 'business of entertainment, media and sports' after being left out of France's World Cup squad.

In 2014 following his retirement, former Manchester United boss Sir Alex Ferguson took up a "long-term teaching position" at the university.

articles.title: Iniciativa pionera del Alcorcón: invita a todos los vecinos de la ciudad al duelo ante el Ibiza
articles.standfirst: El club pone en marcha el proyecto ‘Alcorcón Para Todos’
articles.summary: El club pone en marcha el proyecto ‘Alcorcón Para Todos’
articles.body: La Agrupación Deportiva Alcorcón ha comenzado como un tiro la temporada en el Grupo 2 de Primera RFEF. El equipo dirigido por Fran Justo está en un gran momento de forma y la afición está enganchada al proyecto como hacía tiempo que no lo hacía. Para aprovechar ese tirón, el club ha puesto en marcha la iniciativa ‘Alcorcón Para Todos’, una idea pionera en España mediante la cual la entidad invitará a Santo Domingo a todos los vecinos de la ciudad, de cara al duelo del próximo domingo 25 de octubre ante el Ibiza, que se disputará a las 12:00 h del mediodía. Desde el club amarillo definen la idea, puesta en marcha de la mano de Griffin Core Solutions, patrocinador principal del Alcorcón, como “una medida social sin precedentes con un objetivo claro: que toda la ciudad se vuelque con su equipo y que el deporte local gane protagonismo”. “Se trata de una experiencia piloto y nace con la vocación de consolidar un nivel de vínculo reforzado con la ciudad y sus aficionados. Queremos sentir en Santo Domingo la fuerza de toda una ciudad y demostrar que se puede vivir con aún más cercanía y pasión la relación entre el equipo y Alcorcón”, refieren desde la entidad. El plazo para solicitar las entradas se abre el próximo sábado, 17 de octubre. Primero, para los abonados del club, que podrán retirar ese día dos invitaciones por socio a través de la web oficial del club. Por su parte, al día siguiente se abrirá el registro para el resto de vecinos de la ciudad, que podrán asimismo retirar dos entradas por persona. En el Alcor se espera que ese día sea “una auténtica fiesta del fútbol alcorconero”. Además, el club ha anunciado que también pondrá en marcha “diversas actividades y sorpresas antes, durante y después del partido” para que Santo Domingo pueda vivir una jornada única. Esta disruptiva iniciativa del Alcor tiene algún otro precedente en el fútbol europeo. Desde 2023, el Fortuna Düsseldorf, club histórico alemán que actualmente compite en la tercera división de su país, pero que estuvo en la Bundesliga hace no demasiado tiempo, también invita en ocasiones a sus aficionados a que presencien sus partidos en el estadio. El Alcorcón sueña con llenar Santo Domingo con esta iniciativa, y acercar el club un poquito más a la gente de la ciudad. Tras las seis primeras jornadas, el equipo de Fran Justo ocupa el tercer puesto del Grupo 2 de Primera RFEF y está en zona de playoffs de ascenso a Segunda División. Además, es el equipo máximo goleador de su liga (13 goles), además del único que todavía no ha perdido ningún partido.

articles.title: Man City charges: Mourinho jokes Premier League case will outlast him
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho, long an outspoken critic of Man City’s spending, joked that the Premier League case could outlast him.
articles.body:
Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho joked that he may not live to see the end of Manchester City’s legal battle with the Premier League after the club appealed against a ruling that found it guilty of serious financial rule breaches.

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, as well as three of four charges relating to failures to cooperate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal .

The Premier League said that City used “sham” commercial agreements to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn) over nearly a decade, resulting in inaccurate financial reporting and breaches of spending rules.

Mourinho managed Manchester United from 2016 to 2018 and led them to a second-placed Premier League finish behind Pep Guardiola’s City in 2017-18.

“I would rather laugh about it,” Mourinho said when asked about the case in an interview with Italy’s Corriere dello Sport.

“I think we will eventually get an ending, but we are both in our 60s, and we’ll need to be lucky enough to still be around when the final verdict arrives.

“There will be a verdict, then appeals, then more appeals.”

Mourinho has long maintained that one of his greatest achievements in football management was finishing second behind Guardiola’s side, given their spending power at the time.

The Portuguese manager, now 63, said in 2024 that he had not given up on being awarded a winner’s medal for the 2018 season.

“I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Man City with points and maybe we win that league,” he quipped at a press conference ahead of a Europa League match against United with his then-club, Fenerbahce.

“Then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal.”

The appeal process will be conducted in private, and it remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before it is heard, or whether any punishment would take effect immediately.

City, seeking a sixth successive league win, are top of the Premier League with 15 points from five matches and travel to Liverpool on Sunday.

Holders Arsenal entertain Leeds on Saturday, while United host Tottenham later the same day.

Mourinho’s Real Madrid trail fierce rivals and La Liga leaders Barcelona by six points, with five wins and two defeats from their seven league matches this season.

Both Barca and Real are in action on Saturday, with Getafe and Villarreal visiting, respectively.

articles.title: CFP, ESPN negotiating window extends to next week; no deal is expected, per report
articles.summary: This Friday was the deadline for College Football Playoff leadership and ESPN to reach an agreement regarding a proposed 24-team format, but it appears as if...
articles.body:
This Friday was the deadline for College Football Playoff leadership and ESPN to reach an agreement regarding a proposed 24-team format, but it appears as if any news about the contents of those negotiations will have to wait at least a week.

According to a report by Ross Dellenger in On3 , Friday is the day by which, if no deal has been reached, CFP leadership must make a formal proposal to ESPN, at which point ESPN then has five business days to respond to the offer. That would put the deadline for a decision by ESPN at Oct. 16, though Dellenger notes that could even be pushed back to Monday, Oct. 19.

"This Friday's deadline is mostly meant for the CFP," Dellenger explains. "By Friday, if no deal has been struck (one isn't expected), CFP officials must make a formal offer to ESPN, at which point the network has the aforementioned five business days to respond and continue negotiations."

Should a deal not be reached by Oct. 19, CFP leadership, which consists of the 10 FBS conference commissioners and Notre Dame AD Pete Bevacqua, can bring the 24-team proposal to the open market, where other networks can submit bids for the potential expanded playoff.

Whether or not expansion to 24 teams actually happens will come down to the value television networks place on the additional inventory. A 24-team playoff would necessitate the elimination of conference championship games, which Dellenger now pegs as being worth a combined $300 million across the FBS, up from the $200-250 million figure that has previously been floated. That means any new deal for a 24-team playoff would have to at minimum cover the $300 million in lost revenue from not playing conference championship games.

ESPN already pays $1.3 billion annually for the 12-team playoff. The network reportedly also attributes about $200 million of rights fees to its ownership of various conference championship games, like the SEC's and ACC's. In essence, that gives ESPN about a $200 million head start on other networks interested in bidding, because it's money the network already allocates to college football. Would ESPN be willing to add another $100 million or more on top of that? At least one college football insider, Ralph Russo, believes ESPN has a good shot of doing just that , and retaining exclusive rights to the entire playoff.

Dellenger calculates that raising the annual price of the CFP from $1.3 billion to $1.6 billion would net SEC and Big Ten schools another $3 million per year in media distributions. Is that worth it for what would constitute a wholesale change to the sport?

articles.title: Dos goles de Neymar llevan al Santos a remontar ante el Flamengo y empatar 2-2
articles.standfirst: En la segunda mitad, el técnico del Santos, Cuca, sacó a Neymar del banquillo para tratar de imprimir velocidad al juego
articles.summary: En la segunda mitad, el técnico del Santos, Cuca, sacó a Neymar del banquillo para tratar de imprimir velocidad al juego
articles.body: El Santos remontó ante el Flamengo y logró un empate 2-2 gracias a goles de penalti de Neymar, recién recuperado de una lesión, en la vigésima novena jornada de la liga brasileña. Con este resultado, Flamengo se pone con 61 puntos y se mantiene en primera posición, pero ve reducida a uno su ventaja sobre el segundo, Palmeiras, que todavía tiene que jugar hoy contra el Bahía. Mientras, el Santos, que jugaba en casa, se sitúa en octava posición de la tabla y confirma su ascenso después de rozar la zona de descenso durante buena parte de la temporada. El equipo carioca comandado por Leonardo Jardim dominó la posesión del balón en el centro del campo y logró 10 finalizaciones en la primera mitad del partido, que terminó con goles de Danilo y Lucas Paquetá. En la segunda mitad, el técnico del Santos, Cuca, sacó a Neymar del banquillo para tratar de imprimir velocidad al juego y, en un penalti, el exjugador del Barcelona anotó el primero del Santos. El segundo, también de Neymar y de penalti, llegó poco después y selló una gran participación del jugador después de un mes lesionado. Flamengo llegó al partido con seis victorias y un empate en los últimos siete encuentros, además de estar clasificado para las semifinales de la Libertadores. Santos, por su parte, también vive un gran momento, con cinco victorias consecutivas y dos empates en los últimos siete partidos

articles.title: Swansea City: How Welsh club found their way back as ambition returns
articles.summary: With Swansea City leading the Championship as the EFL returns, BBC Sport looks at how the club has brought back old values and new hopes.
articles.body:
Swansea City's flame burned brightly in the Premier League.

Whether it was Michu, Michael Laudrup, League Cup wins, European nights or simply the stylish brand of football, they packed a lot into seven seasons.

Eight years have now passed since a relegation that brought with it a tightening of belts and a lowering of expectations. Ambition replaced by apathy.

But something is flickering in south Wales.

Swansea lead the Championship as it returns from the international break

And there is a growing sense that a club once renowned for 'The Swansea Way' are heading in the right direction once again.

"You can see the ambition and the ideas are there," says Steve Carroll, editor of the fanzine Swansea Oh Swansea. "People are talking about us in a positive way again."

From Snoop Dogg and Luka Modric, to borrowing Brighton's transfer model and a manager moulded by Jurgen Klopp, this is how they've done it.

Quiz: What has happened so far in the Championship?

The Swans flying high - Reviewing Swansea's start to the season

What have we learned from the Championship so far?

Swansea's relegation hangover has taken a while to clear.

Having been taken over by American businessmen before dropping out of the Premier League, there was little sign of spending their way back to the top.

When exciting talent was unearthed - whether homegrown or bought in - they were invariably sold on to balance the books.

While the likes of Joe Rodon, Oli McBurnie, Dan James and more moved on and up, Swansea would take a step back for every step forward.

"As soon as we could get excited and find ourselves in a reasonable position, then we'd sell a player and it wouldn't be invested back into the squad," adds Carroll.

"Fans would get fed up and the disconnect would come back, and we'd start again."

It took its toll on a string of managers, from Graham Potter, to Steve Cooper and Russell Martin.

There was understandable cynicism, then, when new American ownership arrived in late 2024, promising to review how the club was run.

And while they haven't said much since - showing up in local pubs on matchdays but shying away from interviews - they haven't needed to.

"To be fair, they've delivered," says Carroll of US tech and marketing entrepreneurs Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen.

"When we'd get updates from the last owners, it felt as if we were being gaslighted. Now we can see clearly the ambition."

The pair remain based in the States - chief executive Tom Gorringe the decision-maker on the ground - but aren't hands-off owners, clear with their messaging and plans.

Plans that included the investment that first stabilised finances and then green-lit the biggest squad-spending since relegation.

It hasn't stopped there, with the club set to purchase the Swansea.com Stadium from the local council and plans at an advanced stage to restore the club's academy to top-tier status, as well as further investment into the club's women's team.

'Exceptional' Matos who impressed Modric

"There was a time where I would watch Swansea and I wasn't quite sure what they were, whether that was what I saw on the pitch or the players they were bringing in," former Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff recently told the 72+ podcast .

The seven million views of a Swansea goal in the win over Watford in September on one social media platform alone suggests the eye-pleasing identity has returned.

It is what head coach Vitor Matos promised when he was headhunted for the role 11 months ago, despite having just 12 games as a frontline boss with Portuguese second division side Maritimo.

Worryingly close to the relegation places in November 2025, Swansea used data to identify the individual they needed - leading to the 38-year-old who had worked at Liverpool under Klopp as elite development coach.

His interview was said to have wowed the panel, including Swansea's Ballon d'Or winner in the boardroom Modric, with sources saying the style he promised in his presentations are playing out on the pitch.

Namely a style that fits in with the old Swansea way, but with aggressive work off the ball that has Swansea's on-pitch running data surpassing many second-tier rivals.

And all carried by a personality that has connected with fans and players alike; a quiet, smiling leadership that - even by post-match celebrations alone - has echoes of Klopp.

"He had a really tough job when he came in, in terms of where Swansea were in the table," adds McAnuff, who called their start to the season "exceptional".

"From the minute he went in there he's spoken about the DNA of the football club and wanting to tap into that, stylistically, getting them playing a little more to how Swansea fans would expect."

It has resonated but it has also been effective, style not at a cost of substance - as shown with a defensive record that is best in the division, or the gritty way they came from behind to win at Lincoln City before the international break.

There is a genuine awareness and acceptance at the club that they are by no means the finished article - and a 3-1 defeat at promotion hopefuls Southampton was a reminder of that.

But it is equally clear that there are signs they are moving in the right way.

Klopp's 'connector' - new Swansea boss Matos

Snoop Dogg and Swansea - the story behind football's unlikeliest link-up

Ballon d'Or to boardroom – why Swansea for Modric?

Matos put the fundamentals in place last season, and was then backed this summer to add the extra touches.

Swansea's recruitment - once their biggest strength - has been a major problem for many of their years back in the Championship.

Never able to compete with the biggest spenders, Swansea based their old success on having a good eye for a bargain who could grow with them.

The signs that is back are growing - and not by fluke.

The club have slowly built back up expertise, bringing in Jay Lefevre from Celtic as head of recruitment and Ben Stevens from Crystal Palace as sporting director.

Then there has been the eye-catching partnership with Jamestown Analytics, the data company owned by Brighton chief Tony Bloom that has not only brought success to the Seagulls but also to Hearts in Scotland, Como in Italy and Saint-Gilloise in Belgium.

Swansea are among the clubs to agree a rolling contract with the firm, their one slot for each division opening up after previous partners Ipswich were promoted.

The firm's role is said to be akin to consultancy, adding another layer to Swansea's existing processes, backing up findings and verifying the work of the club's own data systems.

Winger Joseph Opoku and midfielder Elijah Just are said to be examples, first identified by Swansea before the confidence to spend was provided by the firm who are seen as the best in their field.

Both World Cup goalscorers were signed - as was exciting and experienced Canada midfielder Stephen Eustaquio from Porto, and the bargain Bosman capture of new Scotland international Stephen Welsh - in a window that signalled Swansea's growing belief in where they are going.

"You can see the difference," says Carroll. "Before, we would look to the bench and know that changing things would make us weaker. Now the subs change games."

How Brighton attract and develop the best young players ahead of their rivals

Born into Celtic, made at Motherwell, Welsh comes of age with Scotland

Last year's Championship-leading goalscorer Zan Vipotnik has been among those reserves - with former Southampton striker Ross Stewart now fit to add to the support of Adam Idah, with McAnuff noting Swansea are also back to adding goals from wide.

They held on to Vipotnik despite a £10m offer from Hull City, but the sale of midfielder Ethan Galbraith for a similar amount to Stoke City shows that a return of ambition doesn't mean ignoring the economics.

Ownership funds are welcome but far from unlimited, especially when compared to rivals.

Spending has been improved, but the process has been about being smarter rather than bankrolling.

Add in the nature of the EFL's financial controls, it has meant a huge focus on boosting revenue streams beyond the matchday income of a club with a limited stadium capacity in an area where disposable income is almost a quarter below the UK average.

If Modric's arrival as a minority shareholder was about introducing him to the world of football ownership and benefiting from his expertise in return, the other high-profile partnerships were done with business in mind.

Hip-hop star Snoop Dogg and fellow US celeb Martha Stewart's introductions were less about how much they invested and more about growing the brand and helping open doors to new partnerships. Swansea this season brought in record sponsorship deals to go with other significant upticks.

And there is also a partnership with media and entertainment investment giants Shamrock Capital - originally founded by the Disney family and who sold Taylor Swift back the rights to her back catalogue - have also provided significant financial support for long-term plans.

"I don't think anyone is expecting us to go up given some of the other clubs who are going to be fighting for promotion," says Carroll, who says a play-off place is a realistic target. "But you can see we're stronger and we're moving in the right direction, so we're going to enjoy it.

"You can feel the positivity and the optimism is back."

There is a long way to go, but the signs are that - even if they don't make it - Swansea have at least refound their way.

articles.title: El Bellingham de Inglaterra y el del Madrid
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', por Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', por Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Se cierra la ventana FIFA y vuelve LaLiga, con cada mochuelo regresado a su olivo. Algunos contentos, otros no tanto, algunos cansados, otros cansadísimos (Vinicius se ha metido 35.000 kilómetros al cuerpo para dos amistosos en Australia y uno con India, algún día habrá que acabar con esto) y también alguno muy descansado y feliz, repuesto ‘milagrosamente’ en tiempo récord de un “esguince grado tres”, caso Valverde, que podrá estar ante el Villarreal a despecho de aquel impactante diagnóstico. De entre todo lo visto estos días referente al Madrid, lo que más me ha llamado la atención ha sido el gran papel de Bellingham con Inglaterra. Ya lo tuvo en el Mundial. En el Madrid no es lo mismo. Le espera un papel de líder en la armazón del juego adobado con una buena cuota goleadora, pero no termina de romper. He ahí otra tarea pendiente de Mourinho (la una es recuperar a Vinicius o sentarle y tirar de Diomande), al que hoy le pedirá la prensa, me figuro, opinión sobre el paseíto sobre dos ruedas de Mbappé, práctica que él tiene desaconsejada. Tengo curiosidad por saber si algo así está prohibido en el contrato y cuál es la sanción. Pero más curiosidad tengo por saber si Mourinho tiene un plan previsto para conseguir que sus jugadores rindan en sus máximos o los más cerca de ellos, que es la principal tarea de todo entrenador. Yo pensé que el Madrid había hecho un buen mercado con el apuntalamiento de la defensa, las llegadas de Bernardo Silva, Diomande y Espí, e incluso con la renovación de Vinicius. Creí que el descarte de Rodri, decisión que Mourinho asumió tras hablar con él (“sus dudas me hicieron dudar a mi”) significaba que tenía un plan de juego sin él, pero después de siete jornadas de LaLiga y una de Champions el equipo no levanta, y el contraste entre el desempeño de Bellingham en su selección y en el Madrid (y algo parecido se puede decir de Cucurella) hablan de tarea atrasada de Mourinho. Ha regresado menos borde, lo que es muy de agradecer, pero también menos eficaz

articles.title: Herrando: “Ser capitán de Osasuna me haría sentir orgulloso”
articles.standfirst: El defensa rojillo analiza para MARCA el arranque liguero de Osasuna mientras se recupera de una lesión en el aductor de su pierna izquierda
articles.summary: El defensa rojillo analiza para MARCA el arranque liguero de Osasuna mientras se recupera de una lesión en el aductor de su pierna izquierda
articles.body: Jorge Herrando es de los jugadores que hacen falta en todos los equipos. Canterano, cumplidor y con ambición de hacerse indiscutible en el once de Osasuna, el jugador navarro atiende a MARCA durante un proceso de recuperación tras caer lesionado frente al Getafe. Durante su ausencia, el equipo rojillo ha acumulado un bagaje de tres derrotas consecutivas y un empate, además de serias dudas con la imagen mostrada sobre el verde. Pregunta. Tras la lesión sufrida, la primera cuestión es casi obligada, ¿cómo está? Respuesta. Estoy mejor. Ya he pasado los peores días, donde tenía que ir con muletas y casi no podía andar. Voy haciendo más cosas, sudo un poco haciendo ejercicio… Es otra cosa. P. ¿Qué pensó cuando fuiste consciente de la lesión? R. Cuando estuve cedido en el Logroñés tuve exactamente la misma lesión, pero en la otra pierna. Noté lo mismo, como una taba y ya sabía que me había roto el tendón. Más que dolor, sentí una mezcla de angustia y rabia por saber que era una lesión importante. P. ¿Se ve pronto de vuelta? R. Todo está yendo bien y estoy tolerando los ejercicios que voy haciendo. Es verdad que es una lástima que esto me pare en seco justo ahora, después de haber sido titular en los primeros partidos, aunque una lesión nunca viene bien. P. Sobre esas titularidades en el arranque liguero, de los últimos tres entrenadores, ¿es Ramis el que más confianza está mostrando en usted? R. Puede ser. Cada entrenador tiene sus gustos y su forma de jugar, pero con Ramis había empezado jugando y estaba confiando en mí. Yo estoy cómodo y me gusta la idea de juego que quiere para el equipo, así que estoy muy contento. P. ¿Cómo están asimilando la idea de juego de Ramis? R. El entrenador quiere un equipo muy competitivo. Que en presión tras perdida seamos los mejores y en agresividad Más allá de la idea de juego, quiere un equipo competitivo y la manera en la que lo transmite, me gusta. P. El equipo se desinfló tras un buen arranque. R. Los primeros partidos empezamos bien. El resultado ante el Alavés empaña un poco, pero fue un error puntual. Tenemos que trabajar lo que nos está faltando. P. ¿Qué opina de las apreturas del calendario y de los horarios? R. En este nivel es más que posible jugar tres partidos seguidos, sobre todo en mi posición de central. Estamos jugando muchos lunes y horarios malos, pero más para la afición que para el jugador. P. ¿Qué opina de los pitos que se escuchan en El Sadar? R. Yo casi nunca tengo recuerdos de ir a El Sadar y escuchar pitos. La afición está viendo que somos capaces de más e igual no lo estamos dando y nos lo exige. No nos beneficia. Cada uno está en su derecho de pitar. Otros no están de acuerdo y animan. Nosotros no nos queda nada más que hacer nuestro trabajo y hacerlo lo mejor posible para que haya aplausos. P. ¿Qué piensas tú de las redes sociales? ¿Lee la prensa y está al tanto de la actualidad? R. Cuando los primeros años todo va bien y las noticias suelen ser positivas, pues te gusta leerlas, pero llega un punto que obviamente no tan bonito, cuando haces un mal partido, también se comenta. Hay que tomarlo con naturalidad, no todo va a ser bonito. Sí que creo que hay barra libre en eso. Si es una crítica constructiva o una crítica del entrenador, una crítica de alguien que sabe por qué has hecho eso en el partido, obviamente te hace mejorar y lo asumes. Y luego hay críticas que no te sirven para nada. P. ¿Qué recuerdos tiene del agónico final de la pasada temporada? R. La situación fue agónica en los últimos partidos, casi descendemos y entiendo que la gente esté sensible con ese tema. Esa situación a los primeros que ha puesto en alerta ha sido a nosotros. Es un privilegio estar en Primera. Hay que valorar estar en esta categoría. P. ¿Cómo vivió el partido de el Coliseum? R. Sentía que nos podíamos ir a Segunda. Sentí lo que todo el mundo, pero por dos. Fueron momentos muy complicados. Quería que terminase todo. Sabía el resultado de Girona, pero no quería ni mirar. P. Tiene contrato hasta 2030 ¿Cómo ve el futuro? R. Me quedan muchos años de contrato por delante. Me gustaría pasar aquí prácticamente toda mi carrera, con lo que conllevaría de ser capitán. Sería algo que me haría ilusión y estaría orgulloso. Es una motivación para mí. P. ¿Le gustaría ser capitán de Osasuna? R. Parece un tópico, pero es algo que, con la responsabilidad que tiene, me haría estar orgulloso. He tenido buenos ejemplos, si algún día llego a ser capitán.

articles.title: Tony Pulis column: Man City boss Enzo Maresca will be demanding a siege mentality at Anfield
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Manchester City players have a great chance to show unity and togetherness when they travel to Anfield on Sunday.
articles.body:
If I was manager of Manchester City now, after they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, my whole psychology with my group of players this week would encompass one major point:

"No-one is going to like us, but we won't care."

I loved being the underdog and I loved to prove people wrong, and that is what I would demand now - a siege mentality from my squad and supporters alike to prove to people that, irrespective of what is happening off the pitch, on the field and the terraces we respect our club and we are going to fight on.

City will be vilified by everyone else but their players have a great opportunity to show unity and togetherness, starting on Sunday away to Liverpool .

'Supporters at away grounds will be baying for their blood'

When the Premier League returns this weekend, the spotlight will be on one game in particular - at Anfield.

As well as preparing for such a huge match, City's players will be arriving back from international duty and going straight into an off-field fight that has turned into a media frenzy.

The allegations seem relentless with finger-pointing from every Tom, Dick and Harry jumping on the bandwagon in hammering a club that has dominated the Premier League for over a decade.

It feels like every positive gained by City over the period in question and beyond has been smashed into oblivion. Yet, despite all of the above, the club have remained firm in denying all charges.

So, where does this leave Enzo Maresca and his City players as they prepare to take on Liverpool ?

Firstly, although they themselves have not been involved in any of the allegations about the club breaking the Premier League's financial rules, they must understand that supporters at all away grounds will be baying for their blood.

City have become a team that, whenever they play, will provide an opportunity for all critics to attack them, and from all angles - including the frenzied media outlets.

So, as the manager, Maresca must first act to reassure his players that the club is not in any way going to take a step back from defending their own position, and also the position of the players, staff and supporters.

Once that is established, I would then expect every player to concentrate on what they are being paid for, which is to win games.

There should be no distractions or any questions that do not relate to the games they are involved in. No excuses about what is happening off the field would be tolerated, and that would be my final word on the matter.

If the verdict about City breaking the Premier League's financial rules is upheld, it will come at a heavy cost to the club and its reputation.

I feel there needs to be more attention paid to all of these rules, and their fairness, because professional football at the top level is now dominated by massive financial investment.

Even if you just consider player transfers, it's not unusual for around a billion pounds to be exchanged between clubs in England and around the world during each transfer window.

While individual players at the top level are being bought and sold for more than £100m, smaller academies are being plundered by the bigger clubs.

They can hoover up the best young players for much smaller 'compensation' fees, enabling them to polish them up and sell them on later for much more - without any Financial Fair Play rules to regulate how much they profit.

That's one way of dealing with FFP, I suppose, but is it for the good of the game, or the players involved?

Over many years of Premier League governance, clubs have broken the FFP rules that are in place. Some have not been caught yet, I'm sure, but others have and have been punished. It keeps happening, so are the current rules right?

Do we need to try to change them or are we taking a bigger risk by leading clubs to find different ways - or loopholes - to try to break the financial shackles that are currently in place?

The money in our game today is extraordinary and today massive corporations, billionaires and even countries are buying our clubs and want to invest more and more into the product but are not able to.

Gone are the days of local business owners buying their local clubs.

In the Premier League, Tony Bloom at Brighton and Matthew Benham at Brentford are the last men standing and, in the Championship, the Coates family at Stoke City and Steve Gibson at Middlesbrough are among the few to have had a taste of the top flight.

I always see the top clubs having the power financially to remain at the top but it's important there is a way for the smart guys - people like those I named above - at clubs without the big bucks or big histories, to play a leading role in the top league in world football.

At the moment all the negative media attention is on what Manchester City have done wrong but the likes of Brighton , Bournemouth and Brentford have achieved success by being smart, without the 'big club' tag.

It's great to see, but surely the rules need to reward all clubs for being smart. Doing the right thing should give everyone the chance to compete at the highest level.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: Nuno Espirito Santo interview: West Ham boss on their bright start, being back in the Championship and facing QPR
articles.summary: West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo speaks to Sky Sports about their bright start to the season and being back in the Championship. Watch West Ham vs QPR live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Friday night; kick-off 8pm.
articles.body:
A reflective Nuno Espirito Santo, as he looks back on how he has changed as a manager and a person since he was last in charge of a Championship club with Wolves eight years ago.

"There are a lot of things that have changed, the league has got harder. There is more quality. But some things stay the same. We still need hard work, honesty."

It was the win against Wolves at the start of September that kickstarted West Ham's season. They had failed to win in their first three games in August, before a 4-2 victory over Nuno's old club at the London Stadium got things moving.

From there, it was three more wins and a draw before the international break, which saw him collect the Sky Bet Championship Manager of the Month award for September.

"It was an important win [against Wolves]," Nuno says. "It was important for me and important for the players to achieve it. It started against Wolves and it continued to the draw at Millwall."

West Ham's last game saw them fight back from two goals down to draw 2-2 at The Den.

"It was a good reaction from all of us in the second half, a game that didn't start well, but we reacted well in the second half and we finished the game strong," Nuno adds.

"It was a positive for all of us, but I still believe that we should have done things better and tried to achieve a different result.

"It's in the past. Let's try to move forward and focus on what's to come."

Up next for West Ham is a clash at home with QPR on Friday night, live on Sky Sports , off the back of a three-week break.

For Nuno and his squad members not on international duty, it was a chance to relax.

But there were also some nerves in hoping that his players away with their respective nations would come back fit and ready for action.

"It was important for all of us," he says. "It was a very tough schedule, so having these days to not only recover physically but also mentally, of course it was too much time, but normally it is. I feel healthy, which is important.

"We are proud that our players represent their own countries, but always worried because we need them to come back okay. It's important how we receive these players.

"We have only had one day back all together. But the dynamic of the session was good and that the boys that weren't here have reintegrated.

A win over QPR would see West Ham go top of the table ahead of the weekend's fixtures, but Nuno is aware the Championship season is a marathon, not a sprint, and there is still a lot to do.

"We have a lot of things to improve," he says. "It's a squad that is new. A lot of players have joined us.

"I've chased this objective to always be sustainable in our performances, our play. We have major challenges ahead of us."

One thing West Ham seem to have perfected, however, is their set-piece threat. They have scored six of their 22 goals from them already. Centre-back Konstantinos Mavropanos, remarkably, has scored four in his last four.

"They have been so important," says Nuno. "To have players like Dinos [Mavropanos], and Max [Kilman], they are such threats. It's a positive. We also have the delivery and the accuracy.

"But we do need to find the balance between the offence and the defence of them. It takes a lot of time."

West Ham's last home game on a Friday night saw them put Wrexham to the sword with a 6-0 rout. It was one of the most boisterous evenings seen in recent times at the London Stadium.

The atmosphere, Nuno says, will be vital against QPR.

"It's crucial for us," he says. "Our fans have been amazing at the stadium. I hope they're always with us, again, under the lights.

"It's a perfect scenario for us to put in a good performance."

articles.title: FPL gameweek six tips: What to do with Joao Pedro?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Pras gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers in gameweek six.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert Pras gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek six.

Despite being the most sold player of the international break, Chelsea forward Pedro is still owned by about 65% of FPL managers. From a points-per-million point of view he remains one of the best picks in the game, and Chelsea 's fixture run is excellent for a long stretch. Unless manager Xabi Alonso rules him out completely, I would hold and use the bench.

This is a tough week for captaincy. Erling Haaland is away at Liverpool . Cole Palmer is home to Bournemouth . Bukayo Saka has the Saturday lunchtime kick-off at home to Leeds . Bruno Fernandes is at home to Spurs.

Fernandes has the best fixture and the best chance of a big score, but not many own him. Of the rest, you can talk me into any of them. I am leaning safe and sticking with Haaland. Even in a tougher game, if Man City score he should be the one involved.

If I wanted to be different, I would look at Saka or Palmer, both at home. What puts me off Saka is the possible Havertz injury that will impact their attack, plus an early kick-off straight after a long break. What puts me off Palmer is Joao Pedro. If he is not fit, the Chelsea attack suffers, as we saw in gameweek five against Brentford .

For a new buy, yes. The Arsenal defender has a slight niggle from the England camp. Cristhian Mosquera is fit, and William Saliba is on the mend as well, albeit with an unclear timescale for his return. I would not sell him if I already owned him though - he still represents excellent value.

On a wildcard, or with a free transfer though, there are better defenders in the £5m price bracket, in my opinion.

Fulham play all three promoted sides in the next three games. Gonzalo Garcia at £6m is the one I like. He may be on penalties, and the underlying numbers have been better than the FPL returns suggest. Josh King is the other option. His data (0.44 xGI) is strong and the minutes have been good with 90 minutes in three of the first five games.

Not an urgent sell, although there are concerns there from an FPL point of view with his role.

Under Andoni Iraola he is playing as an eight, not as a 10, and not at right-back. That is the worst of the three for route to points. No real attacking threat from the 10 spot, no defensive contribution from full-back. What is left is set pieces and the odd shot from outside the box. I would not rush him out though.

Close to it, at the price. The Brighton midfielder is still under £6m, he plays 90 minutes, and 47 points already explains why he is the most-transferred player this week.

Ownership is about 30%. Sunderland away, then Crystal Palace at home, is a decent run of fixtures. He is just an easy set-and-forget midfielder who keeps playing 90 minutes and keeps trickling points in.

articles.title: La responsable del escándalo de los drones que le robaron protagonismo a Messi rompe su silencio
articles.summary: La empresa Sancor Seguros rompió su silencio tras el escándalo con el espectáculo de drones en el cielo de Buenos Aires en el partido de Leo Messi con Argentina.
articles.body: La empresa Sancor Seguros rompió su silencio tras el escándalo con el espectáculo de drones en el cielo de Buenos Aires en el partido de Leo Messi con Argentina. "Hoy cierra una era en el fútbol argentino. La de Leo. La Pulga. El 10. El capitán que nos hizo ilusionarnos, creer y sentir más orgullo que nunca por esta camiseta. Hay noches que quedan para siempre. Y, una vez más, vamos a estar ahí acompañando", anunció la empresa antes del espectáculo de drones. Después se vio en el cielo "Sancor Seguros" antes que la imagen de Leo Messi, lo que provocó una gran indignación en Argentina y provocó silbidos en el Monumental. Tras la polémica la empresa publicó en su cuenta de Instagram que "llenamos el cielo de luces. Y aprendimos algo: cuando esta Leo, el que brilla es solo él. Los escuchamos. Gracias siempre, Capitán".

articles.title: Una oportunidad para Alba Redondo
articles.standfirst: Regresa a la selección tras casi un año de ausencia y con la mente puesta en Brasil 2027
articles.summary: Regresa a la selección tras casi un año de ausencia y con la mente puesta en Brasil 2027
articles.body: Alba Redondo entró en la convocatoria de la selección española tras la lesión de Vicky López. La futbolista manchega no acudía a una cita del combinado nacional desde la final de la Nations League en 2025, siendo el último de sus 47 partidos internacionales el duelo ante Suecia en La Rosaleda de Málaga en el estreno de Sonia Bermúdez como seleccionadora el 24 de octubre de 2025. La futbolista de la Juventus quiere aprovechar la nueva oportunidad que se le ofrece para convencer al cuerpo técnico en el camino hacia el Mundial de Brasil 2027. La que fuera jugadora del Fundación Albacete, Levante y Real Madrid, campeona del mundo en 2023 en un torneo donde fue claramente protagonista [tres goles, una asistencia y participó en los siete partidos de la selección], dio por cerrada su etapa en el conjunto blanco el pasado 30 de junio tras haber jugado 80 partidos y haber marcado 30 goles. "No fue mi mejor etapa", admitió. La albaceteña, de 30 años, hizo un ejercicio de autocrítica y valoró las opciones de reinventarse pensando en poder defender la estrella conquistada en Sídney en el próximo Mundial de Brasil, en cuya fase de clasificación no ha participado. Alba empezó a construir su nueva versión antes incluso de decidir su futuro. Una vez cerró el curso se fue cuatro días a Mallorca de vacaciones antes de volver a la acción. Empezó la pre-pretemporada Syncrosfera, un centro especializado en rendimiento deportivo, donde pudo combinar descanso y entrenamiento en condiciones de hipoxia, simulando una altitud de alrededor de 3.000 metros. Una semana pensada para preparar el cuerpo antes de afrontar el trabajo específico que vendría después. Sesiones individuales con un preparador físico de lunes a viernes alternadas con el trabajo de psicología deportiva y análisis del juego, rutina que mantiene aún hoy en día. La siguiente decisión que tomó fue cambiar de aires. Tuvo sobre la mesa ofertas del Gotham, Rayadas, Roma y Juventus, decantándose por el conjunto bianconeri, un equipo liderado por el también español Isaac Guerrero, que juega Champions League y donde coincidiría con otras compatriotas como Estela Carbonell, con quien coincidiría en un Levante con el que llegó a ganar el Premio Pichichi en la temporada 2022/23; Júlia Bartel, Cristina Librán o Amaiur Sarriegi, compañera en la selección. Con el '20' a la espalda, dorsal que eligió en memoria de aquel 20 de agosto de 2023 en el que España conquistó el mundo, Alba cayó de pie en Turín. Apenas necesitó 62 minutos para estrenarse como goleadora, siendo la protagonista de un empate salvador ante el Hammarby que permitió a la Juventus continuar en la Champions League; y la autora de un doblete ante la Roma que valdría para conquistar la Serie A Women's Cup. En Italia está siendo utilizada como '9' y cuenta con una continuidad, responsabilidad, liderazgo y confianza que le han devuelto la sonrisa al rostro. Redondo ha disputado hasta la fecha en 13 partidos en todas las competiciones, anotando siete goles y repartiendo una asistencia, participando en jugadas de gol en los últimos cinco encuentros. Números que, sin embargo, no fueron suficientes para que Sonia Bermúdez contara con ella para el doble compromiso internacional ante Estados Unidos. "Nos ha costado mucho tomar la decisión. Por pequeños detalles entran otras jugadoras. Debe seguir trabajando. De una '9' no sólo espero goles, tiene que orientar presión, ser intensa en duelos... Por eso nos hemos decantado por Ornella (Vignola)", justificó la seleccionadora. Sin embargo, la baja por lesión de Vicky López hizo cambiar de parecer al cuerpo técnico y Alba recibió la llamada que tanto esperaba. Desde que debutara con la selección española absoluta el 8 de noviembre de 2018 en un amistoso ante Polonia en Leganés, Alba ha sumado 47 internacionalidades en las que ha marcado 16 goles. La manchega puede jugar como extremo o referencia en punta, ampliando el abanico de posibilidades de la actual campeona del mundo y subcampeona de Europa.

articles.title: El Sevilla pone los cinco sentidos
articles.standfirst: Los hispalenses han ganado solvencia mediante la concentración y la reducción de errores defensivos
articles.summary: Los hispalenses han ganado solvencia mediante la concentración y la reducción de errores defensivos
articles.body: El Sevilla ha encontrado en la concentración una de sus mejores virtudes competitivas. Tras la disputa de las primeras siete jornadas de Liga, el cuadro nervionense suma 13 puntos, tres más que la temporada pasada a estas alturas del campeonato, con el mérito añadido de haber superado ya dos compromisos de máxima exigencia contra el Atlético de Madrid y el Barcelona. La clave de este crecimiento no radica únicamente en el sistema táctico ni en la propuesta futbolística, sino en la drástica erradicación de esos fallos individuales que tanto habían penalizado al equipo en campañas precedentes. Tal como apuntaba La Pizarra de Quintana, algunos de los datos analizados mediante las métricas avanzadas de LaLiga Beyond Stats confirman este cambio de tendencia en el Sevilla. Actualmente, se sitúa como el tercer equipo de la competición con menos errores que terminan en remates a puerta del rival (4). Esta estadística supone un contraste radical respecto al curso 2025-26, en el que, por el contrario, era el tercero peor de la categoría en esta misma faceta (35). La disciplina que ha interiorizado el conjunto que dirige Luis García Plaza se refleja también de manera clara en su propia área de castigo. Si en las siete primeras fechas del ejercicio anterior incurría en 0,3 penaltis por partido -concretamente dos-, en la presente todavía no ha sufrido ninguno en su contra, reduciendo a cero el número de penas máximas cometidas. Por el momento, la fuerza mental de este Sevilla se traduce en una mayor rentabilidad durante los tramos finales de los encuentros. A partir del minuto 80, su balance es de tres goles a favor y apenas uno en contra, amarrando cuatro puntos clave gracias a sus victorias ante el Rayo Vallecano y el Valencia. En ese mismo periodo de la 2025-26, anotó dos tantos y encajó otros dos, lo que le dejó un saldo neutro en cuanto a puntuación. Más concentrado, sobrio y maduro, esta nueva versión demuestra que los hispalenses han aprendido a competir mejor a base de no desconectarse.

articles.title: James McAtee: How Oliver Glasner has transformed Nottingham Forest midfielder from forgotten man to his new Adam Wharton
articles.summary: James McAtee has been one of the most creative players at the start of this Premier League season; Oliver Glasner has turned McAtee into his new Adam Wharton at Forest; watch Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest live on Sky Sports' Super Sunday from 1pm, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
A key part of that set-up are the two central midfielders. "We call them the quarterbacks," said Glasner last season and at Palace. The Austrian had the perfect quarterback in Adam Wharton. Defensively astute but also influential and creative in attack.

As well as finding the Forest version of Wharton, he also had to replace the Man City-bound Elliot Anderson - heartbeat of the team - in that same area of the pitch.

But nobody expected the solution to both these problems to be James McAtee.

Just a few months ago, McAtee was a forgotten man at Forest. Following his £30m move from Man City, he started just two Premier League games last term. All four Forest managers never gave him a real chance.

Glasner has found a role for him at the City Ground - but it has needed a change in position to do it. McAtee, who came through the ranks with City and England as an attacking No 10, has been told to play much, much deeper in this Glasner team.

It is a major change from what McAtee is used to. But even the great Pep Guardiola noticed how good he is in tighter spaces.

"Pep always references how good he is in pockets," said Brian Barry-Murphy to Sky Sports in 2024. Barry-Murphy was one of McAtee's coaches in the Manchester City academy set-up, and is now in charge at Cardiff City.

"What's the most significant thing about James McAtee?" he adds. "The tighter the spaces, the more at home and comfortable he is. He's a very specific player in that role."

And being a small, left-footed talent operating in those tight spaces, McAtee is acting as a pretty good tribute act to Wharton in this new Glasner system.

A key part of Wharton's game is those punchy passes through the lines that open up defences. In the opening weeks of the season, McAtee has been seen doing exactly the same thing - and the results have been excellent.

In the first five games of this Premier League campaign, McAtee has been one of the Premier League's most creative players. Only five players have created more chances this term than the 23-year-old and only three better his creativity from open play.

In terms of passes leading to a shot - balls that eventually bring about an effort on goal within two or three passes - McAtee ranks second in the Premier League, sitting level with Bruno Fernandes, who was the most creative player in the top-flight last term.

Only his Forest team-mate Morgan Gibbs-White has managed more passes leading to a shot than McAtee this season. While Gibbs-White is Forest's talisman, it could be argued that McAtee has the more important role in the team.

Remember, he is in the Wharton role. He is the quarterback.

"They are responsible for the speed of our attacks, if we go forward or keep possession," added Glasner last season about the role.

McAtee is the midfielder who controls the play. Those punchy passes that Wharton and McAtee both make are vital and crucial to Glasner's direct style.

Like at Palace last season, Forest are not interested in passing the ball around. It is a vertical, efficient style that the Austrian manager likes, rather than a patient philosophy.

It is best noticed by the statistic that only four of Forest's attacks this season have been 'build-up attacks'. Put more simply, when they get the ball, they play it forward as quickly as they can. They have the fourth-best record for forward passing percentage this season, while they sit third for the number of through balls completed.

McAtee is at the heart of that style of play. Wharton also dictates that style for Palace. That quickfire ability to generate chances and push the ball forward is why the Eagles midfielder is so highly rated.

So when Glasner makes his much-anticipated return to Crystal Palace, this time in the Forest dugout, there is more than just a simple storyline at play.

This is not just the tale of Glasner returning to the club where he brought unprecedented success to generations of Palace fans. This is not just the narrative of Glasner turning up at Selhurst Park representing the team who replaced them in last season's Europa League.

This is also Glasner's new project coming up against his old one. And in Wharton lining up in midfield up against McAtee, there is a specific battle of 'old vs new' at play here.

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick faces defining month at Old Trafford as Carlos Baleba emerges as potential game-changer
articles.summary: Manchester United face a huge October run; Michael Carrick is under increasing pressure after a difficult start, while Carlos Baleba's return could provide a much-needed boost to United's midfield.
articles.body:
Although Manchester City have dominated the headlines during the international break, it is easy to forget that, given the position Manchester United find themselves in, they could be one more disappointing result away from a storm of questions over whether Michael Carrick is the right coach to steer them through it.

That is why the next week, and indeed the whole of October, feels huge for United.

A home encounter against a winless Spurs side on Saturday is followed by away trips to Atletico Madrid, Leeds United and Como, before the month finishes with Bournemouth and Chelsea.

But on the flip side, this is an opportunity for Carrick and his side to kick-start their season.

The United head coach has pointed to a series of unfortunate events that have contributed to the club's slow start, but there will be less empathy as this next phase of the season begins.

Carrick has been reluctant to address his team's underperformance in his media duties, but he will hope the international break has done his squad a world of good.

The positive is that plenty of players have had time to address their form, fitness and perhaps even their confidence. Matheus Cunha is a good example.

Fair to say the Brazilian has looked slightly off it this season. That may be partly down to playing through the middle rather than in his preferred left-wing position, but with Cunha not called up by Brazil, he has had time to reset after a disappointing start.

The better news for Cunha is that, with Amad Diallo also now fit, Carrick can finally reshuffle an attack that has failed to look threatening despite some impressive offensive statistics.

Amad's return on the right means Bryan Mbeumo can move back through the middle, while Cunha could have a fascinating battle with Marcus Rashford, pending his fitness, for the role on the left.

Carrick has been limited with his attacking options so far, partly because of Benjamin Sesko's lack of availability, but he now has the options to change the look of his side if he chooses to do so.

Friday's news conference with Carrick will be really interesting, not just to hear his thoughts on Manchester City's situation and how he has been impacted as a former player, but because the team news ahead of Saturday's encounter with Spurs will be key.

Carrick does not tend to give too much away in his pre-match news conferences, but with the number of concerns and question marks over his squad, just how many options will he have at his disposal on Saturday?

Noussair Mazraoui and Patrick Dorgu both left their international sides due to injury, while there are still question marks over Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo after they pulled out of England duty, alongside Benjamin Sesko with Slovenia.

Amad, as mentioned, is one. Matthijs de Ligt is getting closer to full fitness, but perhaps even more significant is the pending debut of summer signing Carlos Baleba.

The £65m signing is now fit after suffering an ankle injury for Brighton in pre-season and has had the international break to acclimatise to life at Carrington.

Baleba is understood to have settled into the club well with staff and players and completed his first broadcast commitments as a United player earlier this week alongside Amad, which would point to the midfielder being ready to feature as soon as Carrick believes he is.

The context of Baleba's arrival could have been very different if United had begun the season more positively. Perhaps he could have been slowly introduced into the team.

But after United's start, which has yielded five points from five games, Baleba's importance has only increased in terms of what he can add to this midfield.

The axis of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo has shown us what Carrick thought in pre-season. It feels like the right combination in certain games and certain situations, particularly at home when United are more comfortable dominating the ball and dictating the tempo, but the consistency is not quite there yet.

Baleba will offer this midfield qualities that have still yet to be replaced following the summer departure of Casemiro.

Of course, he will offer physical attributes, but at both ends of the pitch he could really change the fortunes of this team.

Defensively, he will be able to better shield a defence that has, unfortunately, leaked too many goals this season, particularly when United are caught in transition.

But, as I've said since he signed, I am really looking forward to seeing what he can offer going forward too.

During his more impressive spells in a Brighton shirt, he always left me impressed with his range of passing and his ability to drive with the ball through midfield.

Those are qualities United have largely been without in that midfield for years - perhaps since Paul Pogba?

It is too early to say Baleba can be transformative for this team, but for what Carrick and his side need, especially with the games to come, he could prove to be United's most important signing of the summer.

articles.title: ¿Mbappé al Liverpool? La sorprendente respuesta de Daniel Riolo: "Puede ser"
articles.standfirst: El periodista francés de RMC Sport analiza en La Tribu la situación del delantero del Real Madrid y no descarta que busque tranquilidad en Inglaterra
articles.summary: El periodista francés de RMC Sport analiza en La Tribu la situación del delantero del Real Madrid y no descarta que busque tranquilidad en Inglaterra
articles.body: La situación de Kylian Mbappé sigue generando dudas tanto en España como en Francia. Para conocer cómo se está viviendo todo lo que rodea al delantero del Real Madrid en su país, Daniel Riolo, periodista de RMC Sport, ha intervenido en La Tribu, donde ha mostrado su desconcierto y ha dejado abierta la posibilidad de que el futbolista busque un cambio de aires. "Después del verano, debo decir que no entiendo nada de lo que está haciendo Mbappé, sobre todo en términos de comunicación", ha comenzado explicando Riolo. El periodista considera que el problema no está tanto en su rendimiento deportivo como en sus decisiones fuera del terreno de juego. Una de las reflexiones más llamativas de Riolo ha llegado al analizar el estado de ánimo del delantero francés y su posible decepción con el proyecto del Real Madrid. "Muy posible, porque él esperaba un equipo diferente. El equipo es el mismo, con los mismos problemas de la temporada pasada. Cambió el entrenador, pero los problemas son los mismos. Está decepcionado, pero es un jugador del Real Madrid", ha señalado. En ese contexto, el periodista de RMC Sport ha planteado un escenario sorprendente: "Es posible que él busque un poco de tranquilidad en Inglaterra, por ejemplo". Preguntado directamente por la posibilidad de que ese destino fuese el Liverpool, su respuesta ha sido breve, pero contundente: "Puede ser. Porque no me parece que él esté bien. Parece que él está en su mundo y dice, no me importa nada, de los periodistas, de los socios, nada de nada". El periodista francés también ha cuestionado los últimos episodios protagonizados por Mbappé durante su recuperación. "No entiendo nada de lo que hace con el equipo de Francia, que se marcha lesionado y va a la discoteca, con las fotos, con la cámara y después el episodio de la bicicleta", ha explicado. Para Riolo, esa actitud resulta especialmente difícil de comprender en un futbolista del Real Madrid: "Para mí es un problema en un club como Real Madrid decir 'no me importa nada de lo que piensen'. Es un problema porque el fútbol es un deporte popular y tú no puedes decir que no te importa nada de lo que piensa o dice la gente". Además, ha sido tajante al valorar el encaje futbolístico de Mbappé con Vinicius. Aunque ha reconocido que desconoce cómo es la relación personal entre ambos, su opinión sobre la pareja ofensiva es clara: "No es posible que jueguen juntos Vinicius y Mbappé. A mí me parece imposible, imposible". Por último, Riolo ha explicado que en Francia las últimas decisiones del delantero han generado más sorpresa que críticas: "Con este episodio de la discoteca, de la bicicleta, la gente estaba totalmente sorprendida a decir, ¿qué está haciendo? ¿Qué está haciendo?". Un escenario de desconcierto alrededor de Mbappé que, según el periodista de RMC Sport, va mucho más allá de lo estrictamente deportivo.
