articles.title: Mourinho talks Mbappe controversy, Diomande, Valverde, Militao, Mendy, Rodrygo ahead of Real Madrid vs Villarreal
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has defended Kylian Mbappe amid the controversy surrounding the Real Madrid forward’s private life, dismissing the criticism as “ridiculous” an...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho has defended Kylian Mbappe amid the controversy surrounding the Real Madrid forward's private life , dismissing the criticism as "ridiculous" and insisting the Frenchman has fulfilled his responsibilities to the club.

Speaking ahead of Real Madrid's clash against Villarreal, Mourinho addressed the scrutiny surrounding Mbappe's recovery from a knee problem, his recent activities away from Madrid and the possibility of a hostile reaction at the Santiago Bernabeu .

The Portuguese coach also discussed Yan Diomande's potential role, the team's preparations after the international break and several injury concerns.

Mourinho began by acknowledging the difficulty of preparing for Villarreal, describing the opposition as a Champions League-calibre side while highlighting the challenges caused by international commitments.

"The opposition are Champions League calibre. They play very well.

"After losing the last match, we need to pick up points. Preparation isn't easy.

Mourinho has defended Kylian Mbappe. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"Villarreal aren't in the same situation as us, but they've also had players on international duty. It hasn't been the perfect week for them either."

Asked about the growing controversy surrounding Mbappe, Mourinho suggested that the media had been unable to resist creating another major story around Real Madrid.

"If this happens, it'll be a huge victory for you lot. Not even massive stories like the City one or the difficult situation in my country with Cristiano and his manager.

"So many stories that could have fuelled your work, but it hasn't been enough. Real Madrid is Real Madrid, and you always have to make something of it.

"I expected the first one to be the only one based on something real. A difficult match. Yours is the first… But here we are."

Asked whether the fuss had become excessive, he replied: "Over the top? It's ridiculous."

Mourinho then explained why he believes footballers remain accountable for their conduct away from the pitch.

"For me, a player is a player 24/7. Anything important or negative he does privately always has repercussions.

"I always maintain that a player will always be a human being. A man who can make mistakes, but who has a sense of responsibility.

"Everything was perfectly defined. Everyone has complied. The injured players come to Valdebebas immediately. They have their diagnoses, recovery plans…

"Players like Arda, who was suspended for the fourth match, I gave him two unscheduled days off. Players with serious injuries have been here every day. Valverde, Konate.

"The example of Mbappe. He's been here, he's had a diagnosis. He went to an outpatient appointment because his knee has a history that can't be forgotten. Complete agreement between diagnoses.

"And then, there's the realm of problem-finding. The real problems that football has had these past couple of weeks haven't been enough, so there's this search for problems.

"First, the nightclub that wasn't a nightclub. Because it was a venue for a private event during Paris Fashion Week. Then, the bicycle in Switzerland, which was a hotel with small houses. They were bicycles for getting around to common areas in a quiet hotel. And it seems he was doing the Tour de Suisse."

Mourinho backs Mbappe and addresses possible Bernabeu reaction

Mourinho confirms Mbappe will play against Villarreal. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images)

With supporters potentially expressing their frustration, Mourinho refused to endorse the criticism and insisted that players who fail to fulfil their obligations would not be protected from consequences.

"This is one of your objectives. You don't need to be Einstein to realise that this is the objective. As for the person I'd rather not mention – I may be wrong – but he is one of the targets.

"As for the Bernabeu, I won't comment. Out of respect. My hope is that the Bernabeu will be able to be fair. To be fair is to be intelligent. Reading between the lines and understanding the dynamics.

"I promise that if a Real Madrid player doesn't behave like a Real Madrid player and fails as a Real Madrid player – if he doesn't fulfil his obligations as a player or as a citizen – you won't see that player on the bench. You won't be able to boo him.

"He'll be at home. I won't give him the chance to sit on the bench. Mbappe is going to play. He won't even be on the bench. I'm sure he hasn't failed in his obligations to Real Madrid."

Mourinho was also asked whether Yan Diomande could start alongside Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. He declined to reveal his selection but stressed that Madrid must maintain their tactical balance.

"I won't tell you whether he'll play or not. I don't lie, and I'm not going to say who's going to play.

"Real Madrid can field any of the players in the squad up front. We've got plenty of quality players. They can't all play together.

"If you want four forwards, they can. Against Elche, we played with six in the final minutes. But in a balanced situation where risks are managed, we can't play with seven of them together. We can't play with all of them."

Mourinho provides Real Madrid injury update

The Madrid manager also explained how he had planned the squad's return following the international break, taking into account travel, playing time and recovery.

"I spent two or three days in a row after the last match trying to analyse the possible details, so as not to get bogged down in the obvious.

Federico Valverde is a doubt for Villarreal clash. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"I've planned the squad's arrival in detail. Some arrive on Tuesday or Wednesday; some play, others don't; one's jet-lagged, another hasn't slept… It's complex.

"We're working very well in terms of organisation. We could have an injury within ten minutes, but the fact that we don't have any injuries isn't something we forget here. A lot has changed and we're handling it well. We're preparing for the future as best we can."

Asked whether the second half of the season would bring significant tactical changes, Mourinho said the team needed gradual improvement rather than an immediate overhaul.

"In this first period, we've found many good things and things to improve. It doesn't mean we have to change drastically.

"I can't just arrive with one or two days and say, 'Let's start playing with five at the back, four in midfield, and change the full-back.'

Real Madrid is coming off a difficult period. What for others would be a normal situation. We need time to improve things. There are things that improve gradually, and we're doing that."

Finally, Mourinho confirmed that Federico Valverde remained a doubt, while Eder Militao would not feature despite encouraging progress in training.

"Fede is a doubt. Militao isn't a doubt, but he won't be playing. But watching him train the way he does, we've never trained with just five players.

"If you didn't know about Militao's problems, you'd put him in tomorrow. He's better than I thought. He won't be playing tomorrow, nor in Rome, nor against Sevilla. He needs a couple of weeks.

"His medical history is quite serious, and we have to be careful.

"Ferland Mendy will train on the pitch with us for the first time. Rodrygo is still a way off. As for Valverde, the issue has carried over until today. We'll decide today about tomorrow," he concluded.

articles.title: Everton up for sale? Friedkin Group considering new investment options including the potential sale of controlling stake
articles.summary: The Friedkin Group (TFG) have said they will only entertain interest from parties who they feel are the "right stewards to take the club forward"; TFG completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024
articles.body:
The group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin , completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 - ending Farhad Moshiri's long spell at the helm.

The Friedkin Group (TFG) have said they will only entertain interest from parties who they feel are the "right stewards to take the club forward".

"When TFG became custodians of Everton, the club faced significant financial uncertainty and challenges both on and off the pitch," an Everton statement said on Friday.

"The immediate priority was to provide the stability, investment and support needed to secure the club's future, including helping to bring the long-promised stadium to completion for its deserving supporters.

"With that foundation now safely in place, the time is right to consider the next chapter for Everton. We will only entertain interest from parties who we strongly believe will be the right stewards to take the club forward and build on the momentum that has been established.

"Throughout this process, TFG's focus will remain unchanged. We will support the club in all ways necessary to achieve success on the pitch and will continue efforts to make a positive difference in the communities the club serves.

"TFG and the club will not be commenting further while this work is underway."

Why are Everton owners putting the club up for sale so quickly?

"It's not come as a big surprise to hear this news. When The Friedkin Group said a few months ago that they were looking for investors, the feeling and talk around Everton and the financial side of things that the club was actually up for sale. It was a sale they were looking for, rather than investors.

"One of the real reasons for this is TFG have probably come to a point where they have seen what it's going to cost to put Everton back at the top table of English football, which is where the club want to be and where they were a long number of years ago.

"That figure and cost implication is probably too much for them and they don't want to do that.

"From day one, there were rumours and mumblings that TFG weren't going to be at Everton for long. What they've been trying to do recently is put the club into a good financial situation, with a sale in mind.

"A lot of this also comes from the situation with Roma. They own Roma as well, they are building a new stadium there which will cost £1bn. In the end, it's all too much for them.

"I believe The Friedkin Group are looking for between £800m and £1bn to sell the club which will give them a tidy little profit, as they bought the club for cheaper than they should have done.

"It was interesting when you read the statement from The Friedkin Group saying: 'We will be fully committed to supporting the team on the pitch'. Well it didn't look that way in the summer transfer window, that's for sure. It was a bit of a disaster in the end.

"Although you have to remember the squad they had a is a good squad, but a weak squad. If David Moyes was to get injuries with his players, then that squad would be tested. There's no two ways about that.

"The first squad he has at the moment is a very good, strong squad. But you could see that they were willing to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest. That said a lot about the investment and what they were doing.

"The only reason he didn't go was because the crowd made their feelings known. That pressure forced The Friedkin Group to reconsider selling him as he's one of the young bright talents of Everton."

articles.summary: Ligue 1 Predictions, Round 6GFFN editor-in-chief Luke Entwistle, and sub-editor Bastien Cheval face off in our Ligue 1 predictions competition, which returns...
articles.body:
GFFN editor-in-chief Luke Entwistle, and sub-editor Bastien Cheval face off in our Ligue 1 predictions competition, which returns for the 2026/27 campaign. This season, GFFN will also be hosting guests. It's three points for a correct score, two points for a correct score difference, and one point for a correct result. Who will come out on top at the end of the season?

Game of the week: RC Lens v Olympique Lyonnais, Friday 19:45 (UK)

Form is out the window following what was an extended international break. It almost feels like the start to a new season and that will be acutely felt by RC Lens in particular. Just before the international break, they opted for a managerial change, with Yannick Cahuzac promoted from his role of assistant to replace Dino Toppmoller. Cahuzac had very little time to work with his squad before their trip to AS Monaco just before the international break.

He will hope that his principles are taking hold, and Lens will be buoyed by the returns of Yacine Titraoui and Saud Abdulhamid, although the former is not expected to start on his return from a muscular injury. It will be a fresh start after what had been a difficult first few weeks of the season.

In contrast, Olympique Lyonnais are riding high. Just two points off Ligue 1 leaders AS Monaco, they went into the international break off the back of a 4-0 win over Stade Rennais, who are tipped to secure UEFA Champions League football this season. It is a result that did a lot to dispel the growing notion that Paulo Fonseca is not a manager for the big matches, the big occasions. He can further dispel that notion at the Stade Bollaert, although it is always a difficult place to go. It being Cahuzac's home debut as manager only adds further complication.
